rationale: Round-2 duty: classify my round-1 ask (R3-F1 + the derive-level test demand folded into it) against fix commit 3c472ac9, and re-sweep the consumer enumeration. VERDICT ON MY ASK: FIXED, in exactly the preferred one-line form. derive.go's WorktreeSpec backfill is now unconditional (`if ctx.Phase == ""`, the `&& !ctx.DerivationFailed` gate removed), matching the WorktreeBead branch's preserved ModeImplement fallback, with an accurate in-place comment recording why. Traced cleanup.go:50 under a bd outage from a spec worktree: epic lookup fails, the AllEpics health probe fails (with .beads present), DerivationFailed=true is set, Phase is backfilled to "spec", SpecID matches path-derived, so `ctx.Phase != ModeIdle && ctx.Phase != ""` REFUSES — fail-closed restored. The bead-worktree path ("implement" fallback, never broken) and the main-worktree path ("" on error, pre-existing and pre-bead-5-identical) are unchanged, so every branch's Phase value now matches pre-bead-5 semantics and the DerivationFailed doc comment's 'additive, values unchanged' claim is true for every arm. The new internal/phase/derivation_failed_test.go pins the RIGHT sites: its header honestly discloses that the two `phaseErr` branches are defensive-only — I verified that claim directly (DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache returns `nil` error on every path; child-fetch errors are swallowed via `children, _ := c.GetChildren`) — and it exercises the three genuinely reachable sites: WorktreeBead's FindEpicForBead `bd show` failure (asserting DerivationFailed + the unchanged fallback value), WorktreeSpec's AllEpics probe failure (asserting DerivationFailed AND Phase==ModeSpec — this assertion sits directly on the round-1 bug's line, so reverting the fix turns it red), and WorktreeMain's DiscoverActiveSpecs failure (asserting DerivationFailed with the honestly-empty Phase). Each fixture creates .beads explicitly so the failures classify as health failures rather than the uninitialized-workspace idle — the correct precondition. RE-SWEEP: fresh enumeration of every Context.Phase reader outside internal/phase (grep, non-test) yields exactly the round-1 set — instruct_tail.go:30/39 and run.go:161/183/187 (all DerivationFailed-aware; run.go:183 is round-2's G5.2 addition and only executes after the DerivationFailed check above it), cleanup.go:50 (restored fail-closed), hook.go:213 (with values restored everywhere, its behavior is now byte-identical to pre-bead-5 — my round-1 MINOR observation about message-level display stands as a future-bead note, unchanged in weight). The two other grep hits (internal/harness/analyzer.go, internal/resolve/resolve.go:41) read Phase fields of DIFFERENT types (harness events, SpecStatus), not phase.Context — no guard there was ever exposed to the round-1 shape. cleanup.go and hook.go are untouched by 3c472ac9 (verified via diffstat), confirming the fix took the value-restore route rather than growing scope into undeclared files, as asked. Round-2's other additions under my lens: adoptSpecTail routes through emitInstruct (DerivationFailed-aware) and never fails the verb (warning-only), preserving the R1.4 boundary; FormatResult's termsafe.Escape on IndeterminateReason is render-sink hardening with no contract impact; BeadsDirMissing's export (G5.1 licensing disclosed) replaces what would otherwise have been a second drifting copy of the precondition in internal/instruct — a contract-stability improvement, not a risk. Tests: internal/phase, internal/instruct, internal/complete, internal/cleanup all pass in the bead worktree; targeted cmd/mindspec verb-output/tail suites pass under MINDSPEC_ALLOW_MAIN=1 (my environment's globally-installed pre-commit hook, the same round-1 artifact, is the only reason the flag is needed — not the bead). My round-1 forward-compat advisories (R3-F3 bead-6 third-completion-path note, R3-F4 verified-held items) remain accurate and non-blocking.

findings.title: Pre-existing, out-of-scope: DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache swallows child-fetch failures
findings.detail: Verified while checking the test file's defensive-only disclosure: DerivePhaseWithStatusWithCache never returns a non-nil error — `children, _ := c.GetChildren(epicID)` swallows a bd failure into a nil child set, and DerivePhaseFromChildren then derives a phase from it (in the no-stored-phase fallback arm). This is the same fabrication CLASS spec 128 R2.3 targets, at a layer below ResolveContextFromDirWithCache, pre-existing and untouched by this bead — the round-1 ask did not cover it and I am not expanding it in round 2. Worth a spec-128 residual note or follow-up bead if the spec's honesty mandate is meant to reach DerivePhase itself; the new test file's header already documents the shape accurately, so the trail exists.
